captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 8. In this lesson: The lady of the lake, retold.
Compare old-fashioned and modern language in a retold classic tale.
Here are some new words. Retell. Tell a story again in a new way. Archaic.
Very old-fashioned and no longer used. Quest. A long search for something important.
And some more words. Noble. Having good qualities like honesty and courage. Enchanted. Under a magic spell.
Loyal. Always supporting your friends or leader.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: tell a story again in a new way?
Now some grammar: Archaic and modern English.
Older texts use words and structures that are rare today: thee or thou means you, hath means has,
ere means before, whence means from where, and ’tis means it is.
For example: ‘Whence comest thou?’ becomes ‘Where do you come from?’ For example: ‘’Tis a fair morning.’ becomes ‘It's a nice morning.’
Now listen, and read along. The sword in the lake. Long ago, when kings rode out on quests,
a young knight named Gareth came to a still, silver lake deep in an enchanted forest.
His own sword had broken in battle, and he had sworn to find a new one ere the next full moon.
As he knelt to drink, the water began to glow.
A hand rose from the lake, holding a sword whose blade shone like morning light.
A voice spoke from the water: ‘Whence comest thou, and why dost thou seek a sword?’
Gareth bowed. ‘I come from the king's hall,’ he answered, ‘and I seek a sword not for glory,
but to protect those who cannot protect themselves.’ The voice was silent for a long moment.
Then the hand moved closer. ‘Then take it, noble knight.
But remember: the day you use it for yourself alone, it will return to the water.’
Another question. The video will stop. Why did Gareth need a new sword?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like retell, archaic, quest.
You practised archaic and modern English. And you read The sword in the lake. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 8. In this lesson: Why did she do it?
Analyse character motivation and use formal and informal register.
Here are some new words. Motivation. The reason why someone does something. Register.
The level of formality in language. Informal. Relaxed language used with friends.
And some more words. Jealous. Unhappy because someone has something you want. Regret.
Feel sorry about something you did. Consequence. A result of an action.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: the reason why someone does something?
Now some grammar: Formal and informal register.
Formal language is used in official or serious situations, with no contractions and with polite phrases.
Informal language is relaxed, with contractions, slang and short phrases.
For example: Formal: I would be grateful if you could help. For example: Informal: Can you give me a hand?
Now listen, and read along. The stepsister's letter.
Dear Ella, I am writing this letter because I owe you an explanation – and an apology.
When you came to live with us, I was jealous.
Everyone noticed you: your kindness, your singing, the way the birds seemed to follow you.
Nobody ever noticed me. So when Mother gave you the hardest jobs, I said nothing. Sometimes I even laughed.
On the night of the ball, I tore your dress. I told myself it was a joke. It wasn't.
I have regretted it every day since. My actions had consequences that I did not understand at the time.
I do not expect you to forgive me. But I wanted you to know that I am truly sorry. Yours sincerely, Clara
Another question. The video will stop. Who is the letter from?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like motivation, register, informal.
You practised formal and informal register. And you read The stepsister's letter.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
